task: renew a driver's license or vehicle registration on a state DMV portal: verify identity and eligibility, work through the renewal form, pay the fee; complete when the renewal-submitted confirmation — receipt or temporary document — is on screen. Surface pinned: a state DMV web portal, not an in-office visit vlog. Variants: address change (seeded variant), first-time license applications, REAL ID upgrades, and driving-test booking do not belong.

tree.label: Renew a DMV credential online
tree.note: 1 and 2 in the order the venue dictates - account venues meet 3 first and reach the service from the dashboard (DeKE, w74r, _xgB); the rest run 1, then 2, then 3. 2.4 and 2.5 fire before or mid-task as the requirements demand (w74r, YWFI). then 4, with 5 interleaved wherever the wizard asks. 6 only on the carrier systems, then 7 once the approval lands (-eBX, F_2L), then 8. no keeper re-enters an earlier goal by choice - the one reach-back is 7 into 5.8 when a missing email blocks payment (DeKE).

children.label: Find the renewal service
children.note: 1.1 or 1.2 to arrive, then one of 1.3, 1.4, or 1.5 as the venue offers. 1.5 comes after 3 on account venues - the dashboard is behind the login.

questions.question: Does the site handling this renewal identify itself as the official one for your jurisdiction, rather than a general portal or a lookalike?
questions.why: The address bar shows navigation to a specific county tax collector site (pbctax.com) rather than a general state DMV portal, which dictates where the renewal is processed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delegator loses the ability to ensure the agent uses their specific local county portal rather than a general state website.
questions.check: Does the page identify itself as the official government renewal service for this credential and jurisdiction — agency name, official-site banner, or government domain shown on the page?
questions.say_example: I'm on <the county tax collector's site>. That's where <your state> handles renewals, even though it isn't called the DMV.

questions.question: Does the result about to be opened carry the official government domain, rather than a third-party or phishing copy of the agency's portal?
questions.why: Verifying that the search result URL contains the official government domain ensures you are entering the legitimate LTMS portal rather than a third-party or phishing site.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally inspect the URL and confirm that your sensitive identity information will be submitted to the authentic government agency.
questions.check: Do the search results include sponsored or third-party renewal services above the official government domain?
questions.say_example: The top results are paid renewal services that add their own fees. I'm skipping those for the official <state> site.

children.label: Browse the menus to the service
Pick the service from the shortcuts

questions.question: Does the dashboard's renewal reminder name the credential you actually intend to renew?
questions.why: The dashboard displays a specific vehicle renewal reminder alongside multiple menu options like 'LICENSING' and 'VEHICLE'.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the visibility of their dashboard reminders and the ability to personally confirm exactly which vehicle is currently due for renewal.
questions.check: Does the dashboard show a menu option or reminder matching the credential the person asked to renew?
questions.say_example: Opened <Vehicle> renewal from the dashboard reminder.

questions.question: Does your account dashboard show an existing balance that you need to address?
questions.why: The dashboard displays an account balance upon login (e.g., "Balance: ($82.20)"), which could indicate a credit to apply or past due fees to settle before you can successfully renew.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to realize you have a credit on your account or owe back taxes before initiating a new transaction.
questions.check: Does the dashboard display an account balance other than zero?
questions.say_example: Your account shows a balance of <$82.20>. The site may want that settled before the renewal. Should I look at it first?

questions.question: Which registration period do you want to renew?
questions.why: The dashboard lists multiple periods, such as '30-Apr-2019' and '30-Apr-2018', and requires you to select one to proceed with the vehicle renewal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure the correct registration year and associated balance is chosen for your account.
questions.check: Does the page list more than one registration period available to renew?
questions.say_example: There's more than one registration period open here, <30-Apr-2019> and <30-Apr-2018>. Which one am I renewing?

children.label: Confirm eligibility and requirements
children.note: 2.1 where a notice exists - the pages after it repeat what the notice already said (hI3L, 7b3U). 2.2, 2.3, and 2.6 in the order the pages present them. 2.4 and 2.5 whenever the requirements reach into the physical world, mid-task included (w74r, YWFI). then 2.7, with 2.8 wherever a terms gate blocks the path.

questions.question: Do you want to schedule an in-person appointment if the online system cannot process your renewal?
questions.why: The page displayed a banner stating online processing was unavailable due to the expiration date and provided a link to make an appointment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to abandon the online task or proceed with scheduling an in-office visit.
questions.check: Does the page display a notice that online processing is unavailable for this renewal, and does it offer an appointment link?
questions.say_example: The site says it can't renew this online, because <the expiration date is outside the online window>. It offers an in-person appointment instead. Want me to book one?

questions.question: Does the portal indicate any active holds, such as unpaid parking tickets, tolls, or property taxes, that block the renewal?
questions.why: If the system flags a hold, the renewal cannot proceed until it is cleared, which often requires navigating to a different local agency's site to pay the outstanding fine first.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to find out exactly which agency they owe money to and resolve the hold, instead just receiving a generic failure from the agent.
questions.check: Does the page show a hold, stop, or outstanding-obligation notice on the record?
questions.say_example: There's a hold on your record for <unpaid tolls>. The renewal won't go through until that's paid, and it's paid on <a different site>. Want me to take you there?

questions.question: Does the renewal notice say a smog check is required before you can renew?
questions.why: The renewal notice explicitly states that a smog certification is required and provides the website URL and identification number needed to renew online.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the opportunity to personally verify prerequisites like a required smog check before initiating the online renewal.
questions.check: Does the renewal notice state that a smog certification is required before renewing?
questions.say_example: The notice says a smog check is required first. I don't see a passing test on file, and that happens at a station, not here.

questions.question: What details does the renewal notice show, before 'Process Renewal' starts the renewal itself?
questions.why: The IRP Menu displays multiple similar options like 'Process Renewal' and 'Print Renewal Notice', making it important to know which specific link actually initiates the information-gathering step.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the chance to personally review the printed renewal notice and verify your vehicle details before the renewal is processed.
questions.check: Does the menu show a link that starts the renewal process?
questions.say_example: Chose <Process Renewal> from the menu.

questions.question: What specific date ranges do I need to report for my mileage and heavy vehicle use tax?
questions.why: The [name] IRP Application PDF explicitly highlights the required 2021 to 2022 reporting periods for mileage and HVUT that must be used to complete the renewal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the opportunity to personally verify the exact historical reporting periods required for your vehicle's tax and mileage records.
questions.check: What reporting periods does the application document state for mileage and HVUT?
questions.say_example: The application wants mileage for <July 2021 through June 2022>. I'll ask you for the numbers when the form does.

questions.question: Do the conditions for a first provisional license apply to my situation?
questions.why: The screen lists specific criteria for a first provisional license, such as never having applied before or applying before March 1973, which dictates whether you must complete this section or skip it.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally verify your driving history against the portal's specific criteria to ensure the correct application path is chosen.
questions.check: Does the page list criteria for a first provisional licence as a separate section from renewal?
questions.say_example: Skipped the first-licence section. This is a renewal.

questions.question: Do any of these conditions apply to me that would prevent me from renewing online?
questions.why: The screen lists specific conditions, such as needing a road test or an updated medical report, that mandate an in-person visit instead of an online renewal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent might incorrectly assume you are eligible to renew online without knowing your personal medical status or testing requirements.
questions.check: What conditions does the page list that require an in-person visit instead of an online renewal — road test, medical report, eye exam, address change, restricted licence types?
questions.say_example: The site lists reasons you can't renew online, like <needing a road test> or <an updated medical report>. Do any of these apply to you?

questions.question: Should you wait to renew so your new license doesn't say 'UNDER 21'?
questions.why: The portal warns that renewing more than 40 days before your 21st birthday results in an 'UNDER 21' license, which might make you want to delay the process.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to delay their renewal to ensure their new ID does not have underage markings.
questions.check: Does the page warn that renewing more than 40 days before the 21st birthday results in an UNDER 21 licence?
questions.say_example: One thing first. Renewing now, more than 40 days before your 21st birthday, prints <UNDER 21> on the new license. Waiting avoids that. Renew now, or wait?

questions.question: Are you willing to lose the remaining validity on your current license by renewing it today?
questions.why: The portal explicitly warns that the new license will be valid from the date the application is approved, not from the expiry date of the current license, meaning early renewals sacrifice existing validity time.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to delay the renewal until closer to the expiration date to maximize the validity period of their license.
questions.check: Does the page state that the new licence is valid from the approval date rather than from the current licence's expiry date?
questions.say_example: Heads up, the new license starts from the day it's approved, not from your current expiry. Renewing today gives up the <8 months> you still have. Still want to renew now?

questions.question: Do any special renewal conditions, like being 70 or over, apply to you?
questions.why: The screen lists alternative renewal links for specific situations like being 70 or over, driving a bus, or having a medical license, which dictate whether you can use the standard process.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the opportunity to personally verify if your specific age, vehicle type, or medical status requires a specialized renewal path.
questions.check: Does the page list alternative renewal routes for specific situations — 70 or over, bus drivers, medical licences?
questions.say_example: This page has separate routes for some situations, like <70 or over>, <bus drivers>, and <medical licences>. Do any of those fit you? Otherwise I'll take the standard one.

questions.question: Which remote renewal method do you want to use?
questions.why: The notice provides three different options for renewing—by phone, mail, or online—each with specific requirements like a 14-digit authorization number or a check.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to evaluate the requirements for each method and select the one most convenient for your situation.
questions.check: Does the notice list online renewal among the available methods?
questions.say_example: Renewing online. The notice also offered phone and mail.

questions.question: Do you want a standard renewal, or do you need to switch to a REAL ID?
questions.why: The screen requires choosing between a standard renewal and a REAL ID conversion, which dictates the steps and documentation needed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to decide whether to upgrade your standard license to a federally compliant REAL ID during this renewal cycle.
questions.check: Does the page require choosing between a standard renewal and a REAL ID, and what does it say each requires?
questions.say_example: Standard renewal or REAL ID? The page says a REAL ID is what you'll need to fly within the U.S., and upgrading can mean extra documents. Which one?

questions.question: Did you provide the required vision test results to continue with the renewal?
questions.why: The portal explicitly states that an eye test from an approved provider is required, but the session ends without resolving this step.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to successfully complete the renewal because a mandatory eligibility requirement was ignored.
questions.check: Does the page state that an eye test from an approved provider is required, and does it show one on file?
questions.say_example: The site wants an eye test from an approved provider before this can finish. I don't see one on file. That happens outside this site.

questions.question: Do you have the addresses of where you have lived over the past three years readily available?
questions.why: The 'Before you start' section explicitly requires you to provide a three-year address history to complete the driving licence renewal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to gather their complete address history before starting, potentially causing the session to time out while they search for past residential details.
questions.check: Does the before-you-start section state that a three-year address history is required?
questions.say_example: This form will ask where you've lived for the past three years. Have those addresses handy? Tell me now and I'll fill them in when it asks.

children.label: Read the fee and time quotes

questions.question: What does the page say the renewal costs and how long does the new licence last?
questions.why: The screen displays the £14 fee and the 10-year renewal requirement, which are essential facts to confirm before starting the application.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally review the exact cost and eligibility rules before committing to the renewal process.
questions.check: What fee and renewal term does the page state for the online renewal?
questions.say_example: It's <£14>, and the new licence runs <10 years>. The card should arrive in about <a week>.

questions.question: How long will it take to receive your new license?
questions.why: The screen states the license should arrive within a week, which sets expectations for when you will receive the physical document.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the direct reassurance of knowing exactly when to expect your new physical license in the mail.
questions.check: What arrival timeframe does the page state for the new licence?
questions.say_example: New licence expected within <a week>.

questions.question: Do you have the items the site says you need before it will start?
questions.why: The 'Before you start' screen explicitly states that these items are required to create an account and proceed with the renewal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally confirm that you have the required email access and identification documents ready before initiating the state portal process.
questions.check: What items does the before-you-start section list as required to begin?
questions.say_example: Before it starts, the site wants <your license plate and the last five of your VIN>. Can you read those to me? Or point me at the renewal notice.

questions.question: Do you want to accept or reject analytics cookies before continuing?
questions.why: The screen requires you to choose your privacy preferences regarding analytics cookies before you can proceed with the renewal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the ability to control your privacy preferences regarding how the DMV tracks your usage of the service.
questions.check: Does the page show a cookie consent banner with a reject option?
questions.say_example: Said no to analytics cookies.

questions.question: Do you agree to the site's terms of use so the application can open?
questions.why: The screen displays a mandatory terms of use modal that must be accepted to access the renewal system.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means losing the opportunity to personally review and consent to the legal terms governing your use of the DMV portal.
questions.check: Does the page require accepting terms of use before the renewal system opens?
questions.say_example: The site wants agreement to its terms of use before anything opens. I'm agreeing so we can continue.

children.label: Pass the identity gate
children.note: one route per venue: 3.1 then 3.2 on account systems; 3.3 then 3.4 on record-search systems; 3.5 on knowledge-field systems; 3.6 where the authorization number comes off a mailed letter. iV8P switches mid-flow from 3.5 to 3.1. two keepers never get past this goal (7t4w, iV8P).

children.label: Decide to log in or register

questions.question: Do you already have an account on this site, so registering again would create a duplicate profile?
questions.why: The portal homepage requires you to choose between 'REGISTER NOW' and 'LOG IN' to access the system based on your prior account status.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent must know whether you already have an established account with the DMV to avoid creating duplicate profiles.
questions.check: Does the page require choosing between registering, logging in, or continuing as a guest?
questions.say_example: The site wants an account. Do you already have one here, or should I set one up with your email? It also allows guest checkout.

questions.question: Does the user enter their own email or client number and password rather than handing those credentials to the agent?
questions.why: The login screen requires either an email address or an LTO client number along with a password to access the renewal portal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user must share their private login credentials with the agent, compromising their account security.
questions.check: What does the login form require — email or client number, and password?
questions.say_example: The login needs <your email or client number> and your password. The password field is yours. I don't keep it. Tell me when you're in.

questions.question: Did the portal require solving a visual CAPTCHA or image puzzle to access the login screen?
questions.why: DMV portals frequently use visual security checks to prevent automated access, which must be passed before any credentials can be entered.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delegator cannot see if the agent is stuck on a silent visual security barrier rather than a broken link or system outage.
questions.check: Does the page display a CAPTCHA or image puzzle that must be solved to continue?
questions.say_example: There's a picture puzzle here to prove you're human. That one's yours. I'll wait.

questions.question: How do you want to search for your vehicle registration?
questions.why: The portal requires you to select a search type from a dropdown menu, which dictates whether you need to provide a PIN or other identifying details.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might select a search method that requires specific numbers or documents you do not have readily available.
questions.check: What search types does the lookup dropdown list?
questions.say_example: Looked the registration up by <plate number>. That's the option that matched what you gave me.

questions.question: Is this vehicle registered under a personal number or a commercial registration number?
questions.why: The dropdown menu requires you to specify whether the vehicle is registered to a company or an individual to locate the correct records.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the guarantee that the vehicle is being renewed under the correct legal ownership classification.
questions.check: Does the dropdown require choosing between personal and commercial registration?
questions.say_example: Searched under <personal>. It's your own car.

questions.question: Which type of ID will you use, and what is the ID number?
questions.why: The portal requires you to select an ID type from the dropdown and enter the corresponding number to locate your DMV records.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose control over which form of identification is used to access your personal DMV records.
questions.check: What ID types does the dropdown list for locating the record?
questions.say_example: The site wants an ID to find your record, <license, state ID, or passport>. Which one, and the number?

questions.question: What are your vehicle's plate number, category, and code?
questions.why: The 'Plate details' search form requires your exact plate number, category, and code to locate your specific vehicle registration record.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally verify that the correct vehicle plate details are entered to pull up your registration.
questions.check: What plate details does the search form require?
questions.say_example: It wants the plate number plus its <category> and <code>. Those are printed on the plate itself. Can you read them to me?

questions.question: Does the form ask for the exact information the site told you to prepare?
questions.why: The site listed the license plate number and the last five digits of the VIN as prerequisites, which matched the exact fields required on the subsequent form.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to verify that the portal's stated prerequisites match the actual information submitted.
questions.check: Does the form require any field the before-you-start list did not mention?
questions.say_example: The form's asking for something the site didn't mention. It wants <your date of birth>. I have it from you, so I'm filling it in.

questions.question: Does the page require agreeing to the Driver Privacy Protection Act warning before continuing?
questions.why: The portal requires the license plate, owner's date of birth, and a checked agreement to the Driver Privacy Protection Act Warning before allowing you to continue.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the chance to personally read and understand the privacy terms you are legally agreeing to.
questions.check: Does the page require acknowledging the Driver Privacy Protection Act warning to continue?
questions.say_example: Checked the DPPA acknowledgment. It says you're accessing your own record, which you are.

questions.question: Is the registration number entered in the format the page's own instructions specify?
questions.why: The red banner offers instructions that reveal specific formatting rules for entering a Commercial Registration number.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to understand the exact formatting requirements for their specific registration type.
questions.check: Does the page link to instructions with formatting rules for the identity fields?
questions.say_example: Followed the site's formatting rules for the <registration number> field.

questions.question: What identity details does the guest renewal require you to provide?
questions.why: The screen requires specific personal details like your DMV ID, date of birth, and the last four digits of your SSN to verify your identity before you can click continue.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to ensure their sensitive personal information is entered correctly and securely before proceeding.
questions.check: What identity details does the guest renewal require?
questions.say_example: It's asking for the last four of your Social Security number to verify you. I'm entering it now.

questions.question: Does the user read the license and authorization numbers off their own mailed notice rather than passing them to the agent?
questions.why: The screen requires a Driver's License Number and Authorization Number from your physical documents or renewal letter to proceed, and provides a phone number to call if the PIN is missing.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent would need access to your physical ID card and private renewal letter to find the required numbers, or they would have to call the DMV on your behalf.
questions.check: Does the page require an authorization number or PIN from the mailed renewal notice, and what does it say to do without one?
questions.say_example: The site needs the PIN from the renewal letter that came in the mail. I can't see that letter. Can you grab it and read me the number? If it's lost, the page gives a number to call.

questions.question: Does the page warn that a processing fee will be added on top of the base fee?
questions.why: The screen confirms your approval for Safe Driver Renewal and discloses the $30.00 base fee alongside a warning about an additional payment processor fee.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to verify your approval status and acknowledge the upcoming processing fees before committing to the payment phase.
questions.check: Does the page warn that a payment processor fee will be added on top of the stated base fee?
questions.say_example: The <$30> here isn't the final number. The site says the payment processor adds its own fee, and it doesn't say how much yet.

children.label: Verify and complete the record
children.note: 4.1 where the account lists vehicles; 4.2 on the fleet systems. then 4.3 against the notice, the insurance, and the inspection. 4.4 to 4.7 as the venue's record demands - document validation on LTMS, insurance on OkCARS, mileage on the carrier systems. 4.8 where the wizard asks for addresses; 4.9 only on licence renewals, where the form asks about the person rather than a vehicle.

questions.question: Did any red error text or warning icons silently appear next to a field when you tried to advance?
questions.why: Form validation errors often appear visually next to the offending field without an audible alert or a change in screen focus.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delegator cannot see the in-line visual cues indicating exactly which field is formatted incorrectly and blocking the submission.
questions.check: Does the page show error text or warning icons next to any field after attempting to advance?
questions.say_example: The form flagged an error next to <the insurance field> and didn't announce it. Fixing it now.

questions.question: Did the search return your correct vehicle, and is it selected for renewal?
questions.why: The screen displays registrations matching your search criteria, so you must verify the correct vehicle is checked before moving on to select the renewal type.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally confirm that the correct vehicle from your profile or search was selected for renewal.
questions.check: What vehicle does the page show as found and selected — plate, make, model, and the period being renewed?
questions.say_example: Found your <Honda, plate ABC123>, renewing through <April 2027>. That's the one I'm working on.

questions.question: Which of your listed vehicles do you want to renew, or is your vehicle missing from the list?
questions.why: The screen requires you to select a specific registered vehicle to renew or indicate if it is not listed, which determines if you can proceed online.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to ensure the correct vehicle is selected for renewal or to learn that unlisted vehicles require an in-person visit.
questions.check: Does the page list more than one vehicle, or none matching the one the person named?
questions.say_example: Your account lists <three> vehicles. You said the <Honda>. That's the one I'll pick. Right one? Or if it's not the one you meant, say which.

questions.question: Do you want to renew all active vehicles from your previous registration?
questions.why: A modal dialog requires you to confirm whether you want to carry over all previously registered vehicles into this renewal session before making individual changes.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means the agent decides whether to bulk-import your previous vehicles for renewal, potentially complicating the process if you only intended to renew a single specific vehicle.
questions.check: Does the page show a prompt asking whether to carry over all previously registered vehicles into this renewal?
questions.say_example: It's asking whether to carry over all <12> vehicles from last year. If any are gone from the fleet, we should drop them now so you don't pay for them. All of them, or should I read the list?

questions.question: Are the vehicle details the page shows for this unit still correct?
questions.why: The portal provides an update button to review and modify specific vehicle details like the unit number and unladen weight before finalizing the renewal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the opportunity to verify or correct specific vehicle details on file, potentially resulting in an inaccurate registration.
questions.check: Does the page provide an update option for the vehicle's details?
questions.say_example: Reviewed <unit 4>'s details. Nothing needed changing.

questions.question: What is the current status of the vehicles you are renewing?
questions.why: The 'Vehicles' tab displays the vehicle's status as 'Pending', confirming it is correctly queued in the renewal supplement before you enter reported distances.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally verify that the correct vehicles and VINs are included in the renewal process before moving forward.
questions.check: Does any vehicle on the list show a status other than pending or queued for renewal?
questions.say_example: One truck isn't queued. Its status reads <Suspended>, not Pending. It won't renew with the others.

questions.question: Are your retrieved vehicle, insurance, and test details accurate?
questions.why: The screen displays your specific vehicle model, insurance policy, and test results, which dictate whether you are eligible to proceed with the renewal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally verify that your insurance and inspection records were correctly reported to the DMV before submitting the application.
questions.check: What vehicle, insurance policy, and test results does the record screen display?
questions.say_example: Pulled the record for <the Honda> - insured with <policy 4471>, test results current.

questions.question: How many power units are you renewing this year?
questions.why: You must verify that your fleet details, such as the physical address and expiration date, are correct before entering the number of power units to renew.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to catch outdated account information or incorrect mileage reporting status before the renewal is processed.
questions.check: Does the page require entering the number of power units to renew, and what count did last year's registration carry?
questions.say_example: It wants the number of power units renewing this year. Last year was <14>. Same again, or a different number?

questions.question: Is all the information for your new license correct before proceeding?
questions.why: The screen warns that the displayed details will be printed on your new driver's license, so you must verify they are accurate.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might not know if your address or endorsements have recently changed, potentially resulting in an inaccurate license being printed.
questions.check: What details does the page show that will be printed on the new licence?
questions.say_example: This is what prints on the new license: <your name>, <the address on file>, <no restrictions>. If any of that's off, it goes on the card that way.

questions.question: Does the printed address on the license preview match your residential address?
questions.why: The license preview shows a Tallahassee address instead of the Fort Myers residential address you entered, contradicting the rule that the residential address must be printed on the license.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user risks receiving a non-compliant driver's license with the wrong address printed on it.
questions.check: Does the address on the licence preview differ from the residential address entered or confirmed earlier?
questions.say_example: Stop a second. The card preview shows <a Tallahassee address>, not the <Fort Myers> one you gave. If we continue, the license prints the wrong address.

children.label: Validate the inspection and insurance documents

questions.question: Does the pre-filled MVISR number match your inspection report?
questions.why: The screen displays an auto-populated MVISR number that must be validated to ensure the correct emission test results are attached to your renewal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally verify that the system pulled the correct inspection report for your specific vehicle.
questions.check: What MVISR number does the page show pre-filled?
questions.say_example: Inspection number came pre-filled as <MV-88231>. That's what the state has on file.

questions.question: Is the pre-filled Certificate of Coverage number correct?
questions.why: Verifying the automatically populated COC number ensures that the correct emission test results are linked to your renewal application.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to verify that the system pulled the correct emission certificate for your specific vehicle before proceeding.
questions.check: What Certificate of Coverage number does the page show pre-filled?
questions.say_example: Coverage certificate pre-filled as <COC-3310>.

questions.question: Are your required documents showing a successful validation status?
questions.why: The screen displays yellow refresh icons next to the inspection report and certificate of coverage, indicating their validation is still pending.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to ensure your mandatory vehicle documents are fully accepted by the system before proceeding.
questions.check: Does any required document show a pending or failed validation status?
